status: pre-registered after the smoke, before the full runs
question: Is e651's coverage of the norm-and-cosine-preserving reflection by the activation-consistency detector an artifact of scoring the edited weights against the clean model's states (X0, A0 computed once before any edit), which a blind auditor does not have?
design: e651's battery unchanged (Pythia-160m, Pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, SmolLM2-135M; block 4; the same corpus, rows (seed 651), edits and clean-model thresholds); every edit scored by consistency twice: with the clean states (e651's, reproduced) and with the edited model's own states, its threshold the 1st percentile of the edited model's own distribution. Norm z-score and read-write cosine need no states and are unchanged.

hypotheses.C1: reproduction: with the clean states, the consistency flag rate on high-use reflections is within 0.15 of e651's on every model (0.67, 0.80, 0.12, 1.00)
hypotheses.C2: the artifact: pooled over the four models, consistency with the edited model's own states flags high-use reflections at most half as often as with the clean states
hypotheses.C3: the defender's reading fails: with the edited model's own states, high-use reflections are flagged by some detector in fewer than half of the rows on at least three of the four models
hypotheses.C4: the analytic premise: the block's MLP activations are unchanged by an edit of its own write (all edits, tolerance 1e-4), so own-state consistency compares the new write with the state minus the old write

context: Found while building the live demo (manifold/wdd_demo.py): its Act 3 sweep on Pythia-410m's 40 most-used block-4 rows caught 0.17 of reflections with own states against 0.33 with clean states, where e651 recorded 0.80.
